previous_goal_turn_classification: verified progress: canonical one-cut actual norm comparison for arbitrary noncoplanar deletions and exact average deletion count
current_goal_turn_classification: progress: exact modified-profile affine transport, actual all-frame reflection extrema, and a proved finite block-label maximum theorem with uninstantiated Wilson block hypotheses
scope: Exact plaquette frames are constructed for every spatial translation and coordinate permutation on even period N=2*n. Reversed orientations use the actual SU(2) inverse-character defect identity. The plaquette permutation, Haar-preserving field symmetry and kinetic interaction are carried together. Arbitrary signed inhomogeneous coupling profiles are transported exactly: actions, weights, actual finite temporal-network densities and coarse Haar partitions agree. Compact positive endpoint growth gives equality of the actual raw modified transfer norms for temporal beta>=0, without any modified ground-state hypothesis. Explicit finite deletion sets and their cardinalities move with the profile. Conjugating the canonical copies proves the actual square norm inequality, average deletion-count conservation, priced Schwarz inequality and nondecreasing reflection choice at every affine spatial cut. At a global maximum of the actual finite Wilson priced norm, both copies at every frame retain the maximum. A maximum minimizing any natural-number rank exists; minimizing deletion count yields an actual maximizer whose two copies have exactly the same count at every frame. Separately, exact nearest-neighbor variation of finite block labels on an even three-dimensional torus is proved to decrease in average under a cut, strictly if the cut crosses a disagreement. Zero variation is equivalent to a constant label, and affine label symmetries preserve variation and move any disagreement to the canonical seam. The finite combinatorial chessboard maximum theorem is proved: a nonnegative score on finite labels, invariant under those affine symmetries and satisfying the literal half-copy Schwarz inequality, is bounded by a constant-label score. For binary labels the bound is max(empty score,fully marked score). The geometric extremal theorem has explicit hypotheses; it has not yet been instantiated with a concrete Wilson block deletion encoding. The fully disseminated quantitative model bound, arbitrary-cluster per-defect suppression, actual distant mixed-ground sum, independent global coercivity, physical scaling, nonzero continuum survival and all twelve full Clay requirements remain open.

notation.fine_period: The actual frame results hold on N=2*n, n>0. The proposed cell instantiation will use fine period 4*n and coarse block-label period 2*n.
notation.push_profile: push(F,gamma)(p)=gamma(F.plaquettes.symm(p)); its actual weight is the original weight evaluated on the framed field.
notation.framed_copy: Transport the deleted set into the canonical frame, apply its literal half-copy, and transport back.
notation.priced: ||T_cut(S)||*exp(-a*s*card(S)), where s>=0 is retained spatial coupling, beta>=0 the independent temporal coupling, a arbitrary real.
notation.variation: The number of disagreeing nearest-neighbor block-label edges on the even spatial torus.

research_sources.use: The finite extremal reflection strategy informs this construction. The new combinatorial statements are proved in Lean, with all score hypotheses explicit; no literature theorem is imported as an axiom or asserted to discharge the remaining Wilson block encoding.

not_inferred: All twelve full Clay requirements remain open. No continuum Yang-Mills construction or cutoff-uniform physical mass gap is claimed.

The actual modified Wilson action and norm now transport through every affine spatial frame. The actual arbitrary-set reflection inequality is valid at every resulting cut; no coplanarity assumption or reflected modified ground state is inserted.

The block-label chessboard maximum theorem is a proved finite combinatorial theorem with explicit nonnegativity, affine-invariance and half-copy Schwarz hypotheses. A concrete Wilson block deletion family satisfying those hypotheses has not yet been encoded and verified.

The existence of an actual priced-norm maximizer, equality of its copied maximum values and count balance do not identify its geometry or give a numerical norm bound. The block-label variation argument is not silently applied to arbitrary plaquette sets.

The next candidate family deletes all six internal plaquettes of selected 2-by-2-by-2 vertex cells on fine period 4*n. This whole-cell choice is intended to preserve coordinate-permutation symmetry; the encoding, copy/transport identities, disjointness and cardinality are still to be proved.

Even after that instantiation, the completely disseminated model must be quantitatively compared with the original full model, and arbitrary marked patterns must be covered with a bounded geometric loss. Connected-cluster entropy and the actual source-weighted activity still require proof.

The distant mixed-ground sum or appropriate signed physical replacement and independent retained-region coercivity, including global gauge/toron directions and source-dependent boundaries, remain open.

Physical scale matching, normalized reflected-state compactness and nonzero renormalized continuum survival remain separate. Finite-regulator norm comparisons and combinatorial reflection theorems do not settle them.
